sections.heading: Matching tenses
sections.body: The tense of the main verb determines which subjunctive tense you use after *que*. This is called *la correlación de tiempos* (sequence of tenses).

sections.heading: Exceptions that make sense
sections.body:
When the past trigger refers to something **still true or still in the future now**, the present subjunctive is possible — very common in Latin America: *Me pidió que lo llame mañana.* (He asked me to call him tomorrow — tomorrow is still ahead.) The standard *que lo llamara* is always correct.

The conditional can take either depending on meaning: *Me gustaría que vinieras* (standard). *Sería mejor que vengas* is heard in some areas but is less standard — prefer *vinieras*.

sections.heading: Putting it together
sections.body:
- *Espero que hayas dormido bien.* (present → earlier: present perfect subj.)
- *Esperaba que hubieras dormido bien.* (past → earlier: pluperfect subj.)
- *No creo que lo sepa.* / *No creía que lo supiera.*
- *Te lo digo para que lo sepas.* / *Te lo dije para que lo supieras.*
- *Busco a alguien que lo haya hecho antes.* (someone who has done it before)

examples: I would like you to come.
I was glad you had come.
I was hoping you had slept well.
Te lo digo para que lo sepas.
I'm telling you so you know.
Te lo dije para que lo supieras.
I told you so you'd know.
Busco a alguien que lo haya hecho antes.
I'm looking for someone who has done it before.
Me pidió que lo llamara mañana.
He asked me to call him tomorrow.
El jefe exigió que resolviéramos el problema.
The boss demanded that we solve the problem.
Le he pedido que me dé permiso.
I've asked him to give me permission.
